claim: For the independent distinguishable-walker model and Meyer--Wallach site-mode quantity of Goyal and Chandrashekar (arXiv:0901.0671), let \(p_{ij}\) be the probability that walker \(i\in\{1,\ldots,M\}\) occupies lattice site \(j\) after \(t\) steps, and use the source's subsystem count \(L=2t+M+1\). Under the product configuration law in its Eq. (26), the single-site purity factorizes exactly as \(\operatorname{tr}\rho_j^2=\prod_{i=1}^M[p_{ij}^2+(1-p_{ij})^2]\). Consequently the source's Eq. (24) satisfies the universal finite-time bound \[E_{\mathrm{MW}}(t)\le \frac{2^M}{2^M-1}\frac{2}{L}\sum_{i=1}^M\left(1-\sum_j p_{ij}^2\right)\le \frac{2^M}{2^M-1}\frac{2M}{2t+M+1}.\] Thus, for every fixed \(M\), the open-chain spatial entanglement quantified by this prescription necessarily tends to zero as \(O(t^{-1})\), independently of the coin parameters and of the detailed one-particle probability profiles, provided the source's independent-walker/product-distribution assumptions hold.
integrity: The all-parameter statement follows analytically from exact factorization of the source's configuration probabilities and the inequality \(1-\prod_i(1-x_i)\le\sum_i x_i\). Exact-rational enumeration is supplementary and not used as an infinite proof.
scientific_limitations: The theorem assumes the independent distinguishable-walker product configuration law of the source.
The source's subsystem count \(L=2t+M+1\) is used as printed; no separate indexing correction is claimed.
No sharpness theorem, matching lower bound, interacting-walker extension, or alternative entanglement measure is claimed.
The originality search is targeted and may miss an equivalent bound stated under different multipartite-entanglement terminology.
title: Universal inverse-time ceiling for open-chain quantum-walk spatial entanglement
